newsitem.title: CHINA: H-SHARES IN HK LIFTED BY RESTRUCTURING HOPES.
newsitem.headline: H-SHARES IN HK LIFTED BY RESTRUCTURING HOPES.

text.p: Shares of Hong Kong-listed Chinese enterprises, or H-shares, made strong gains on Tuesday boosted by hopes of industry restructuring which would improve the earnings outlook of these mainland companies, brokers said.

"Speculation that restructuring plans in some industry may be concluded at China's upcoming 15th Party Congress, has fuelled hopes of a better outlook for Chinese enterprises," said one sales manager at a local brokerage.
The Communist Party Congress is expected to be held in September or October.

The Hang Seng Chinese enterprises Index rose 70.93 points, or 5.22 percent, to close at 1,428.61 at midsession, outperforming the blue chip Hang Seng Index which gained 45.12 points, or 0.27 percent, to 16,505.59.
Shares of Guangdong Kelon Electrical Holdings Co Ltd, which topped the net gainers list, rose HK$0.70 or 7.14 percent to HK$10.50 at midday.
Brokers said speculation that shipping and petrochemical industries would be targeted for restructuring boosted demand for stocks in the sector.
Guangzhou Shipyard International Co Ltd gained HK$0.60, or 18.6 percent, to HK$3.825. Shanghai Hai Xing Shipping Co Ltd rose HK$0.30 to HK$6.75.

Tianjin Bohai Chemical Industry (Group) Co Ltd surged HK$0.60, or 26.67 percent, to HK$2.85, Beijing Yanhua Petrochemical Co Ltd was up HK$0.50, or 22.73 percent, at HK$2.70, and Yizheng Chemical Fibre Co Ltd gained HK$0.30 to HK$4.625.
